note: Generated by scripts/generate-ai-guide.R. Review an entry by editing it and setting status to reviewed.

dictionary.note: What ids and column names mean (cd2030.core::cd_dictionary()). Read meanings from here, never from spellings.

denominators.label: UN projections
denominators.meaning: The UN estimates of live births and population (UN projections). National only.

denominators.label: DHIS2 projections
denominators.meaning: The population projections in DHIS2 (live births, total population, under-1s).

denominators.label: ANC1-derived
denominators.meaning: Derived each year from that year's reported ANC1 visits and the survey's ANC1 coverage: pregnancies = ANC1 / ANC1 survey coverage, then deliveries, births and infants from them.

denominators.label: Penta1-derived
denominators.meaning: Derived each year from that year's reported Penta1 doses and the survey's Penta1 coverage: infants = Penta1 / Penta1 survey coverage, then births, deliveries and pregnancies from them.

denominators.label: ANC1 population growth
denominators.meaning: The ANC1-derived value of the survey year, carried to the other years with the population growth rate of the chosen population (not re-derived from each year's ANC1).

denominators.label: Penta1 population growth
denominators.meaning: The Penta1-derived value of the survey year, carried to the other years with the population growth rate of the chosen population (not re-derived from each year's Penta1).

grammar.meaning: The number of services or events reported for the indicator (a count).
Coverage of the indicator (%) with that denominator option.
The target population (thousands) as estimated by that denominator option.
The same population carried from the survey year with population growth (the population-growth options).
The indicator's coverage in the survey (%).
The upper bound of the survey estimate's confidence interval (%).
The lower bound of the survey estimate's confidence interval (%).
Reporting rate of that service group (% of expected reports received).

populations.label: Pregnancies
populations.meaning: Expected pregnancies: the denominator of the antenatal care indicators.

populations.label: Deliveries
populations.meaning: Expected deliveries: the denominator of institutional deliveries and caesarean sections.

populations.label: Total births
populations.meaning: Expected births, live and stillborn (DHIS2 denominator of BCG, live births, low birth weight, PNC).

populations.label: Live births
populations.meaning: Expected live births (ANC1- and Penta1-derived denominator of BCG, live births, low birth weight, PNC).

populations.label: Live births
populations.meaning: Live births in the DHIS2 projections (the base of the DHIS2 denominators).

populations.label: Infants eligible for Penta
populations.meaning: Infants surviving the neonatal period: the denominator of Penta, PCV, rotavirus, IPV, OPV, zero-dose, under-vaccinated and the Penta dropouts.

populations.label: Infants eligible for Measles 1
populations.meaning: Infants surviving to the age of Measles 1: the denominator of Measles 1 and its dropouts.

populations.label: Children eligible for Measles 2
populations.meaning: Children surviving to the age of Measles 2: the denominator of Measles 2.

populations.label: Total population
populations.meaning: Total population in the DHIS2 projections.

populations.label: Children under 1
populations.meaning: Children under 1 in the DHIS2 projections.

reportingRates.meaning: Reporting rate, antenatal care (% of expected reports received).
Reporting rate, institutional deliveries (% of expected reports received).
Reporting rate, vaccination (% of expected reports received).
Reporting rate, outpatient (% of expected reports received).
Reporting rate, inpatient (% of expected reports received).
Reporting rate, all services (mean) (% of expected reports received).

definition.what: The internal consistency ratios (ANC1/Penta1, Penta1/Penta3, and OPV1/OPV3 for immunization) each year, with the share of districts whose ratio is in the adequate range.

definition.what: Recomputes adjusted_data from data_with_excluded_years and the k-factors, and marks the data as adjusted.

The adjusted numerators: data_with_excluded_years with each count corrected for incomplete reporting with k (reporting rates below the cutoff replaced first) and extreme outliers replaced; carries each indicator's median, MAD and outlier flag. Every coverage, mortality, utilization and health-system result is computed from it.
definition.grain: one row per district x year x month

adjusted_data.question: Gets countdown data with K-factors applied. Adjusts automatically if flags are met.

definition.what: Whether the data have been adjusted (TRUE once Adjust data has run with the current years and k-factors).

adjusted_flag.question: Gets boolean representing if adjustments are active.

definition.what: What the adjustment does: the years removed everywhere, an area's data removed for some or every year (its services and population), and each indicator's completeness k, outlier and missing-value correction -- everywhere, or with a region's or district's own settings (a district's win over its region's).

adjustment_settings.question: The Data Adjustment page's settings (see adjust_service_data()). When none are stored, they are made from k_factors and excluded_years.

definition.what: The yearly numbers of every indicator as reported (after the years and areas removed) and after each step of the dataset's adjustment: completeness, outliers, missing values (the adjusted numbers).
definition.grain: one row per year

adjustment_values.question: The yearly numbers as reported and after each step of the dataset's adjustment (completeness, outliers, missing values), for every indicator. Computed once and kept.

definition.what: The estimates of the Bayesian models already fitted at an admin level, as one table: coverage by year from 2010 to 2030, in percent, with the 95% and 80% intervals, for each indicator fitted with the denominator selected now (a row per region at admin level 1). The Bayesian model already fitted for an indicator (by get_bayes_model() or kept with keep_bayes_model()), or NULL: nothing is fitted.

definition.what: Sets `adjusted_data`: The adjusted numerators: data_with_excluded_years with each count corrected for incomplete reporting with k (reporting rates below the cutoff replaced first) and extreme outliers replaced; carries each indicator's median, MAD and outlier flag. Every coverage, mortality, utilization and health-system result is computed from it.
Sets `adjusted_flag`: Whether the data have been adjusted (TRUE once Adjust data has run with the current years and k-factors).

Sets `adjustment_settings`: What the adjustment does: the years removed everywhere, an area's data removed for some or every year (its services and population), and each indicator's completeness k, outlier and missing-value correction -- everywhere, or with a region's or district's own settings (a district's win over its region's).
Sets `area_survey`: The survey estimates by area of residence (urban, rural): built in, or uploaded.
Sets `cache_path`: Where this dataset is saved: the path of its .rds file (the saved copy the app works on).
definition.set_on: Load Data (Finish writes the saved copy)

definition.what: Sets `chart_options`: What the user changed about how charts look: the dataset's default options and each chart's own, by chart id.
definition.set_on: the chart options menu of every chart

definition.what: Sets `countdown_data`: The HMIS data as loaded: for each district and month, the service counts, the reporting rates (anc_rr, idelv_rr, vacc_rr, opd_rr, ipd_rr) and the population and health-system figures, merged from the uploaded sheets. Nothing is removed or adjusted in it.
definition.set_on: Load Data (Finish merges the uploaded sheets)
